page.title: Device
page.purpose: Show one device's probed capability matrix, its host node and transport, its strategy options, and its session history.

priorities.statement: The capability matrix distinguishes available, unavailable, and unsupported without collapsing them.
priorities.notes: Unsupported is terminal; unavailable is fixable. Merging them hides the actionable case.

priorities.statement: Which strategy would be selected, and why, is visible before any run starts.
priorities.notes: Strategy selection determines which resolution rungs are reachable, so it must not be implicit.

priorities.statement: Host node and transport are shown, because reachability depends on them.
priorities.notes: An attached device is only as reachable as the node it hangs off.

states.description: A reachable device with a current capability snapshot.
Device record and latest snapshot loading.
The device is known to the fleet but has never been probed, so the matrix has no verified rows yet.
Some capabilities are available and others are unavailable or unsupported. The expected state for every strategy except the reference class.
The snapshot predates the probe interval; every row is labelled as last-probed rather than current.
The device or snapshot request failed; the page says so rather than rendering an empty matrix.
Host node offline; the exact reason is displayed and no verb controls are offered.
A capability probe is in flight; the prior snapshot is shown as stale rather than blanked.
A lease is held on this device; holder and expiry are visible.

elements.name: Capabilities
elements.description: One row per optional capability with its declared value, its probed value, and — when unavailable — the missing prerequisite.
The per-capability disposition chip. Renders available, unavailable, or unsupported verbatim; never a checkmark.
Why a capability is terminally unsupported on this transport, distinct from a fixable prerequisite.

elements.name: Selected strategy
elements.description: Which strategy would drive this device and the reasoning that chose it.
The explanation behind the selection, expandable before any run starts.
Host node and transport, since reachability is a property of the pair rather than of the device.
The exact reason the host node cannot be reached, shown in place of verb controls.

elements.name: Probe
elements.description: Re-run the capability probe for this device.

elements.name: Sessions
elements.description: Prior leases and their verb counts, retained past expiry as the accountability record.

elements.name: Live session
elements.description: The same global lease alarm rendered on every route.

claims.statement: Available, unavailable, and unsupported are presented as three distinct outcomes rather than two.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. Unsupported is terminal and unavailable is fixable; collapsing them into 'missing' hides the only actionable one. Manual because it is a three-way perceptual distinction rather than a presence check.

claims.statement: An unavailable capability shows the prerequisite that would make it available.
claims.rationale: D-002 requires a named prerequisite and next action rather than a bare disposition.

claims.statement: The selected strategy and the reasoning behind the selection are perceivable before any run starts.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. Strategy selection determines which resolution rungs exist, so an implicit choice makes every downstream result unexplainable.

claims.statement: Host node and transport are shown alongside the device's reachability.
claims.rationale: Priority 3. An attached device is only as reachable as the node it hangs off, so the pair must be legible together.

claims.statement: When the host node is offline, verb controls are not offered; the reason is shown instead.
claims.rationale: Offering a control that cannot succeed produces a failure the operator has to interpret. Naming the reason is strictly more useful.

claims.statement: The unreachable state renders a dedicated explanation rather than an empty matrix.
claims.rationale: DVC-P0-003 requires the exact reason to survive to the surface.

claims.statement: A probe in flight is perceivably different from a completed probe, and the prior snapshot remains readable during it.
claims.rationale: Blanking the matrix during a probe would make the page unusable exactly when the operator is waiting on it.

claims.statement: A device that has never been probed is perceivably different from one probed and found to have no optional capabilities.
claims.rationale: D-002 at the device scale. ios-mirror legitimately probes to zero optional capabilities; that is a finding, not an absence of data.
